newsitem.title: MEXICO: Changes at Televisa boost share price.
newsitem.headline: Changes at Televisa boost share price.

text.p: Grupo Televisa SA stock shot up at the start of trade on Tuesday in a positive response to the changes in the Mexican media giant's management team and better-than-expected fourth quarter results, market watchers said.
Others said the stock had been undervalued due to a recent slump on uncertainty over the health of its hugely influential leader, Emilio "The Tiger" Azcarraga Milmo, 66 years old.
Televisa said late Monday that Azcarraga was stepping down for health reasons.

Azcrraga will remain as honorary founding chairman, but Televisa will now be run by a team led by his son, Emilio Azcrraga Jean, and the highly respected Guillermo Caedo White, whose experience is seen offsetting any doubts on the younger Azcrraga, who is believed to be 28 years old.

"There was some uncertainty over the possible changes in the management team, and this change is very positive," Martn Lara, a media analyst with Caspian in Mexico City, told Reuters. "Guillermo Caedo White is very positive for the company. He's been involved in their most important dealings."
Caedo was named chairman and chief corporate officer, while Azcrraga Jean becomes president and chief executive officer.

In Mexico City, Televisa stock was up 4.80 centavos or 4.99 percent to 101 pesos after the first 90 minutes of trade. The stock had been as high as 111.10 pesos on January 15, but tumbled after rumors that Azcrraga suffered a heart attack hit the markets on February 13.
Televisa has never been specific on Azcrraga's health problems.
The stock zigzagged later in February, rising at times on a larger market rally.
In New York, Televisa ADRs were up 1-5/8 to 25-5/8.
"In the United States, it's rising because the results were a little better than expected," said one Mexico City desk trader. "I'm going to go in and buy."

Although the company reported a net loss in 1996 of 598.51 million pesos, Televisa still had a positive operating profit of 1.042 billion pesos. Its net losses were due mostly to financing costs because of its dollar-denominated debt in a year of a stronger peso.
In the fourth quarter, Televisa's operating margin was 16.9 percent, well above market forecasts.
One New York-based analyst said Televisa's recent slip made the stock undervalued.
"It (Tuesday's rise) is on the results of a quality company," said the analyst, who asked not to be identified. "Some of the recent fall was unwarranted."
